parsed.why: Enforced sodomy law plus appearance-based arrests: trans women jailed five years for wearing women's clothing, gendarmes beating detainees, police extortion, prison described as 'hell', no lawyers, thin recourse. State-directed targeting on top of universal criminal exposure.

Decriminalised 2021 and no state targeting, but no anti-discrimination or recognition law; police dismiss trans assault complaints over male ID markers, impunity for anti-trans violence, healthcare discrimination. Hostility with thin recourse, no criminal statute.

Working protections: marriage, self-ID, hate-speech law, attackers convicted; no visitor-facing restriction. Offset by documented police mistreatment of trans sex workers, a mob assault, and 63% of respondents avoiding public affection. Social hostility with functioning remedy.

State-run universal exposure: 299 detentions including a street sweep of 20 trans women for ID checks, prison segregation and isolation, a trans prisoner dead in custody, official 'family/morals' criminalisation push. Efficient institutions enforcing hostile policy.

No criminalisation, 2007 ruling and third-gender markers, but document reform lags, trans people harassed in provincial cities and state offices, conversion therapy practiced, care scarce, official hate speech. Protective doctrine, weak implementation, thin recourse.
